title: Broker finder fee payable only by the engaging party
requirement: A licensed broker or salesperson may contract with only one side, and any fee for finding a rental dwelling may be charged only to the landlord or tenant who originally engaged and contracted with that broker.
coverage_conditions: Licensed brokers and salespersons who contract to find rental residential real property for a prospective tenant or to find a tenant for a landlord.

applicability.other: applies to licensed brokers and salespersons engaged by one party

quoted_span: Any fee shall only be paid by the party, lessor or tenant who originally engaged and entered into a contract with the licensed broker or salesperson.

title: Notice to quit for nonpayment must include prescribed form
requirement: A landlord's written notice to quit for nonpayment of rent must be accompanied by a form giving any repayment agreements, rental assistance program information, court rules and any relevant eviction restrictions.
coverage_conditions: Residential tenants given a written notice to quit for nonpayment of rent under chapter 186.
penalty: No court may accept a writ, summons or complaint for filing in a residential nonpayment eviction without proof of delivery of the form.
quoted_span: A notice to quit for nonpayment of rent given in writing by a landlord to a residential tenant pursuant to this chapter shall be accompanied by a form that shall include, but not be limited to: (i) documentation of any agreements between the tenant and landlord for the tenant to repay the landlord for nonpayment of rent;

title: Fair Chance in Housing Act, no criminal-record inquiry before conditional offer
requirement: A housing provider may not ask about an applicant's criminal record on the application or orally before making a conditional offer, except for methamphetamine production in federally assisted housing and lifetime sex offender registration.
coverage_conditions: Applicants for rental dwelling units offered by a housing provider, excluding a unit in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.

applicability.other: excludes a dwelling unit in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units

exemptions: Inquiry allowed as to conviction for drug-related criminal activity for manufacture or production of methamphetamine on federally assisted housing premises and lifetime sex offender registration.
penalty: Director may impose a monetary penalty of up to $1,000 for a first violation, $5,000 with one prior violation in five years, and $10,000 with two or more prior violations in seven years.
quoted_span: A housing provider shall not require an applicant to complete any housing application that includes any inquiries regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to the provision of a conditional offer, except that a housing provider may consider whether an applicant has ever been convicted of drug-related criminal activity for the manufacture or production of methamphetamine on the premises of federally assisted housing, and whether the applicant is subject to a lifetime registration requirement under a State sex offender registration program.

title: Fair Chance in Housing Act, records barred and conviction lookback periods
requirement: A housing provider may not consider arrests without conviction, expunged, pardoned, vacated, sealed or juvenile records; after a conditional offer only listed convictions within set lookback periods may be weighed.
key_value: 6 years first degree, 4 years second or third degree, 1 year fourth degree
coverage_conditions: Applicants for rental dwelling units offered by a housing provider, excluding a unit in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.

applicability.other: excludes a dwelling unit in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units

exemptions: Convictions for murder, aggravated sexual assault, kidnapping, arson, human trafficking, certain sexual assaults and crimes requiring lifetime sex offender registration may be considered without time limit.
penalty: Director may impose a monetary penalty of up to $1,000 for a first violation, $5,000 with one prior violation in five years, and $10,000 with two or more prior violations in seven years; withdrawal requires written reasons and an individualized assessment.
quoted_span: A housing provider shall not, either before or after the issuance of a conditional offer, evaluate an applicant based on any of the following types of criminal records: (1) arrests or charges that have not resulted in a criminal conviction; (2) expunged convictions; (3) convictions erased through executive pardon;

title: Fair Chance in Housing Act, drug and alcohol testing barred
requirement: A housing provider may not require an applicant to take a drug or alcohol test or ask the applicant to consent to release information from a drug abuse treatment facility.
coverage_conditions: Applicants for rental dwelling units offered by a housing provider, excluding a unit in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.

applicability.other: excludes a dwelling unit in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units

penalty: Director may impose a monetary penalty of up to $1,000 for a first violation, $5,000 with one prior violation in five years, and $10,000 with two or more prior violations in seven years.
quoted_span: A housing provider shall not require an applicant to submit to a drug or alcohol test, or request the applicant’s consent to obtain information from a drug abuse treatment facility.

title: Fair Chance in Housing Act, eviction ground after successful provider appeal
requirement: If a housing provider wins an appeal of a director's order, that determination is grounds to evict the former applicant occupying a unit under the order, but only after at least 45 days' notice.
coverage_conditions: A former applicant residing in a rental dwelling unit owned by the housing provider as a result of a director's order that was overturned on appeal.

applicability.other: applies only to a unit owned by the housing provider occupied under an overturned director's order

quoted_span: then a determination that the housing provider did not violate the provisions of this act as evidenced by such successful appeal shall be grounds for the housing provider to evict the former applicant if that person resides in a rental dwelling unit owned by the housing provider as the result of the director’s order, so long as the housing provider provides the applicant with at least 45 days’ notice prior to the eviction
interaction: Applies notwithstanding any provision of the Anti-Eviction Act, P.L.1974, c.49, to the contrary.

title: Residential rental application fee cap of $50
requirement: A landlord or agent may not charge an application or similar fee to lease or sublease a residential rental property that exceeds $50, a limit adjusted annually in proportion to CPI changes.
coverage_conditions: Residential rental property leased or subleased for dwelling purposes, excluding one- and two-family dwellings offered for rent.

applicability.other: excludes one-family and two-family dwellings and real estate licensees who are not the landlord

exemptions: A dwelling unit in a one-family or two-family dwelling offered for rent, and a licensee of the New Jersey Real Estate Commission unless the licensee is the landlord of the property.
penalty: Up to $500 for a first offense, $750 for a second offense and $1,000 for each subsequent offense, enforced by summary proceedings; the amount wrongfully charged is remitted to the applicant.
quoted_span: A landlord, or agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which exceeds $50.
